title: Waste salt separation by antisolvent crystallization process: Mechanism study of Na2SO4-NaCl-solvent ternary phase diagrams and its life cycle assessment
summary: This paper investigates the antisolvent crystallization (ASC) method for separating Na2SO4 and NaCl from industrial pyrolyzed waste salt, including a mechanism study and life cycle assessment. Methanol was identified as an effective antisolvent, achieving high purity and yield for both salts. Ternary phase diagrams elucidated the preferential crystallization of Na2SO4 due to solubility differences in methanol-water systems. The study concludes that the ASC process, with methanol recovery and reuse, offers excellent economic and environmental feasibility for waste salt reutilization.
